subject: Unfinished stream charges and backfill policy
messages:
From: Tom Evans <tom.evans@mediacare.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question on charges for interrupted streaming sessions and retries

Hi Aisha,

We're running an internal proof-of-concept with Redwood streaming responses. A few of our devs noticed that when a client disconnects mid-generation (e.g., network blip or user cancels) the session sometimes resumes and we see partial completions billed. Can you confirm how billing works for these partial/unfinished streams? Specifically: 

- Do we pay for tokens produced before the disconnect only, or are there scenarios where a resumed generation results in additional charge beyond what was already consumed?
- How are repeated retries (client SDK reconnects/resends) accounted for? Is there any automatic deduplication or a backfill credit if the same prompt results in repeated partial outputs?

We're also trying to map this back to our procurement team — any short explainer or rate-card excerpt that covers streaming edge cases would be helpful.

Thanks,
Tom
Director of Platform Engineering
MediaCare Health
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Evans <tom.evans@mediacare.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on charges for interrupted streaming sessions and retries

Tom — thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up front and then a short policy summary attached. Attaching: RD-Hosted-API-Ratecard-v2.pdf and streaming-billing-matrix.xlsx.

Short answers:
- Baseline: we bill for tokens that are successfully emitted by the model (i.e., sent over the wire). If a generation is interrupted mid-token stream, you are billed for the tokens that were delivered.
- Resumes/retries: if a client reconnects and re-requests the same generation, the new tokens produced in the resumed session are billed as well. We do not automatically merge two partial outputs into a single charge or dedupe tokens across separate requests.
- Backfill/credits: we provide discretionary credits in a few cases (service-side interruptions, platform bugs, or clearly duplicated generation attempts caused by server-side retries). Client-driven retries (replays from the customer side) are treated as new usage unless we confirm a Redwood-side fault.

Practical guidance in the attached matrix: it maps common failure patterns (short disconnect, long disconnect, repeated reconnect flood) to our recommended handling and whether a credit is typical. A couple of highlights:
- Short disconnects (<5s) with immediate auto-reconnect: usually no credit; billed for union of tokens emitted.
- Long reconnects where the server resumed a generative state that re-emitted overlapping content: may be evaluated case-by-case.
- If you see repeated identical requests within a short window (client retry storms), talk to us — we can evaluate and often offer a one-time credit while you tune the SDK retry logic.

If it helps for procurement, we can produce a one-page summary that you can attach to your SOW. If you want the engineering nuance I cc'd Aditya (runtime) and Lauren (pricing) to confirm the edge-case wording.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Evans <tom.evans@mediacare.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on charges for interrupted streaming sessions and retries

Looping in with a short engineering note to make the billing behavior more explicit for the matrix. TL;DR: billing events are tied to successful token emission events at the transport layer. A few implementation notes you can share: 

- Each token chunk we emit is timestamped and tracked by request_id. If a second request is issued with the same prompt but a new request_id, we treat it independently for billing.
- We don't attempt cross-request KV cache reconciliation for billing (that would create a lot of complexity when customers intentionally alter prompts mid-session).
- For customers doing migration/testing, we can set a temporary: "pilot-mode" flag on your account that suppresses billing for up to N minutes per session and then provides an aggregated usage file for audit. That is a controlled option we enable per-customer and is visible in the console.

Suggested script for commercial: 
"For pilot migrations, Redwood can enable a pilot-mode waiver for the first 72 hours of a migration window (or up to a predefined token cap). During this window, we provide usage logs and apply a one-time credit for obvious duplicate generation storms identified by our telemetry"

I'll let Lauren weigh in on how that maps to discounts/credits in paper.

- Aditya
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Tom Evans <tom.evans@mediacare.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on charges for interrupted streaming sessions and retries

Aisha — thanks, that helps. Two follow-ups: 

1) Our procurement will want a clear fallback: if our integration tests generate duplicate requests during a 48-hour migration window, what credit level can we expect? They don't want ambiguous case-by-case adjudication.

2) For our pilot we expect a lot of short disconnects as clients with older devices reconnect. Is there a way to request that pilot-mode be tuned to automatically not bill for retries that happen within a 3s window of the prior token stream?

We'd prefer a clear, auditable rule we can put in an appendix to the SOW rather than discretionary credits.

—Tom
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Evans <tom.evans@mediacare.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on charges for interrupted streaming sessions and retries

Tom — understood and reasonable ask. Proposed commercial commitment we can include in the SOW appendix (draft language below). I'm attaching the final ratecard excerpt as well.

Draft appendix language (for your procurement):
- Pilot waiver: Redwood will enable "pilot-mode" for MediaCare Health for a 72-hour pilot window tied to Deal RD-9876. During this window Redwood will suppress billing for repeated client-initiated reconnects that meet the following criteria: same request_id or exact prompt, reconnect interval <= 3 seconds, and total duplicate emitted tokens <= 2x tokens of the original request. Redwood will provide a reconciliation CSV and apply a one-time credit corresponding to the suppressed usage.
- Guaranteed credit threshold: If automatic suppression identifies duplicated tokens meeting the above criteria, Redwood will apply a credit equal to the suppressed token cost up to a cap of $2,500 for the pilot window.
- Escalation path: any questionable cases will be reviewed within 3 business days by Redwood's Billing Ops; the review will reference telemetry logs and the supplied request_ids.

Commercial tradeoff: To offer the above we request a short-term pilot commitment (non-binding) to move to a 3-month paid sandbox at negotiated pilot rates if the integration proceeds. Lauren — can you confirm the pilot-rate and discount we should offer here?

Thanks — if that language looks good to you I can get it into our standard SOW appendix and share with procurement.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
